title: The Tree That Wore SNAKESKIN (Then Became Coal) 🐍
description:
Is this a snake or a tree? A tree: a scale tree (Lepidodendron), up to about 40 metres tall, from the coal swamps of about 300 million years ago. Every diamond on its bark is a leaf cushion: the spot where a leaf grew, then fell off. When whole swamp forests of them fell into the water, they didn't rot away. They were buried, squashed and slowly cooked into coal: in some North American coal swamps these trees were about 70% of all the plant matter. Steam engines burned that coal by the ton. And miners still find their stumps standing in the rock above the coal seams. They call them kettlebottoms, and they can drop out of the roof without warning. Snake or tree: what did you guess?

Fun fact: the name of their age, the Carboniferous, means "coal-bearing". (The idea for this one came from a viewer's comment: thank you!)
